harmonicFunction: E5 (I) - Rock tonic providing huge low-end power and open string chime
C#m7 (vi7) - Minor submediant adding emotional bittersweet gravity
Aadd9 (IVadd9) - Subdominant chord with ringing open high B and E strings delivering uplifting dream-rock warmth
Bsus4 (V) - Suspended dominant chord building energy before resolving home to E

techniques.name: Melodic Octave Riffing & Open-String Chime
techniques.description: Fretting octave intervals on the 5th (A) and 3rd (G) strings while muting the middle D string with the pad of your index finger

notes: Octave shapes: E (7th fret A, 9th fret G), C# (4th fret A, 6th fret G)
Muted D string: Let your index finger lean lightly against the 4th string to silence it completely
Open string resonance: Let strings 1 and 2 ring open during chord transitions
sequence: Position index finger on fret 7 of A string, pinky on fret 9 of G string
Rest the underside of your index finger on string 4
Slide smoothly down to fret 4 (C# octave) and into open E power chords
tips: Octaves require firm fretting pressure on the active strings but zero tension in the right wrist
Dave Grohl and Pat Smear layered multiple guitars (Gibson Trini Lopez into Mesa Dual Rectifier and Vox AC30) for thickness
Lock into the slow, pounding 77 BPM groove—don't rush

techniques.name: Stadium Dynamic Explosion & Ringing Open-String Power Chords
techniques.description: Balancing quiet, palm-muted verse power chords with monumental open-string chorus explosions across E5, C#m7, Aadd9, and Bsus4

notes: Open-string voicings: C#m7 (X-4-6-6-0-0), Aadd9 (X-0-2-2-0-0), Bsus4 (X-2-4-4-0-0)
The open B and high E strings create a continuous shimmering harmonic drone
Dynamic attack: feathered palm-muting in verses contrasted with full-arm arena downstrokes in choruses
sequence: Palm-mute the low E5 power chord in eighth notes during the verse
Keep open B and high E strings vibrating lightly across chord changes
Stomp distortion pedal right on beat 1 of the chorus ('There goes my hero')
Deliver full, wide downstrokes letting the wall of sound reverberate
tips: Do not mute strings 1 and 2 during the chorus chords—they are the key to Grohl's massive stadium sound
Keep your fretting wrist straight to avoid fatigue during extended power chord holding
Listen to the rolling tom drums to anchor your internal 77 BPM clock
details.progression: E5 - C#m7 - Aadd9 - Bsus4 Chorus Cycle

sections.name: Intro Octave Hook & Rolling Drums
sections.description: The driving octave hook cutting through Dave Grohl's iconic rolling tom drum intro.
notes: Keep the middle D string muted cleanly
Slide smoothly between frets 7 and 4
Dig in with aggressive pick strokes

sections.name: Verse 1 Palm-Muted Power Chords & Ringing Strings
sections.description: The verse rhythm under 'Too alarming now to talk about' moving between E5, C#m7, and Aadd9.
notes: Light palm muting on the bass notes
Let the high open strings breathe
Maintain the heavy 77 BPM pulse

sections.name: Chorus 1 Stadium Wall of Sound ('There goes my hero')
sections.description: Massive wall of sound on 'There goes my hero, watch him as he goes'.
notes: Open strumming with maximum dynamic energy
Let high E and B strings ring open across all shapes
Hit the crash on beat 1

sections.name: Verse 2 Melodic Octave Counterpoint
sections.description: Dave Grohl layers the opening octave hook over the second verse rhythm for added emotional lift.
notes: Crisp articulation on the A-string notes
Damp the D string with the index finger flesh
Lock into the slow-motion drum groove

sections.name: Bridge Acoustic Breakdown & Crescendo Build
sections.description: Quiet breakdown with gentle acoustic strumming swelling gradually into the final chorus climax.
notes: Soft acoustic strumming building in pick intensity
Open high strings shimmer as guitars layer in
Explode into full distortion on the final chorus drop

sections.name: Chorus 2 & Final Resonant Power Cadence
sections.description: Thunderous double chorus followed by the rolling drum and octave outro cadence dying down into feedback.
notes: Maximum power chord downstroke velocity
Allow the open high strings to ring into natural amplifier sustain
Let the final low E chord ring out to natural silence

guitar.recommended: Gibson Trini Lopez Standard / Gibson DG-335 (Pelham Blue)
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker (Burstbucker / Gibson Dirty Fingers) for maximum crunch

amp.recommended: Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier blended with Vox AC30

effects.distortion: ProCo Rat distortion or Boss DS-1 (for extra chorus bite)
effects.delay: Subtle analog delay on lead lines

beginner.title: Chorus Power Chords
steps: Learn the open power chords: E5, C#m7 (fret 4), and Aadd9
Practice steady eighth-note strumming at 77 BPM
Focus on the dynamic transition from verse to chorus

intermediate.title: Octave Riffing Technique
steps: Master the A-and-G string octave shape with index and pinky
Ensure the middle D string is completely muted with no unwanted notes
Slide smoothly between the 7th and 4th fret octaves in time with the drums

advanced.title: Dynamic Control & Stadium Energy
steps: Perform the entire song with full dynamic control from delicate verse to roaring chorus
Lock tightly with the drum roll groove without rushing the 77 BPM tempo
Replicate the layered dual-amp tone (Mesa crunch + Vox chime)

commonMistakes: Letting the middle D string ring open during octave slides
Rushing the tempo during the heavy drum intros (stay locked at 77 BPM)
Over-strumming during the verse instead of maintaining tight palm muting
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Octave muting drill on strings 5, 4, and 3
5 minutes: Octave slide timing at 65 BPM → 77 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus open chord dynamic strumming
metronomeWork: Practice the octave riff with metronome at 77 BPM
Focus on landing the octave slide down to fret 4 exactly on beat 1
